steps.narration: Velox brings your delivery life cycle into one workspace. In this walkthrough, you'll turn a discovery call transcript into a complete business requirements document.

beats.caption: Head to Velox via URL: ai-labs.deluxe.com/sdlc/login

steps.narration: Start at the Velox login page and sign in with your Azure AD account. Authentication runs through your organization's single sign-on, so there's no separate password to manage.

beats.caption: Login using SSO

steps.narration: You land on the Velox workspace. The left rail holds the modules available to you: architecture, pair programming, testing, deployment, drift alignment, and more. And in the center is the Velox agent.

beats.caption: You've now landed on Velox

steps.narration: First, choose a project.

beats.caption: Select your project

steps.narration: Open the selector at the top to pick an existing project or create a new one.

Creating a project takes three inputs: a name, a BRD template, and a link to Atlassian. The Jira project and Confluence space are required because that link is what gives every session inside the project real context to work from.

beats.caption: You can create a new project
by linking to the Jira project & Confluence space
Or proceed by selecting an existing project

steps.narration: With the project set, open the BRD assistant from the left menu.

beats.caption: Head to the BRD Assistant Module

steps.narration: Each project holds its own set of BRD sessions.

beats.caption: ..and start a new session

steps.narration: Start a new one, and Velox asks a single question first:
Should this session carry forward the project's accumulated context or begin clean? Choose Start fresh when you're exploring a new angle rather than continuing earlier work.

beats.caption: Create a fresh session

steps.narration: Velox names the session for you from your first message or document.
Next, choose how to begin. You can start with a conversation and describe the project in your own words.

beats.caption: You can begin with a conversation with the BRD Assistant

steps.narration: Or you can start from documents and upload what you already have: a conversation transcript, an existing BRD, or a template.

beats.caption: Or start by uploading a transcript or BRD template

steps.narration: Here, I'll upload a transcript from a discussion with the payments team.
Mary, the strategic business analyst inside Velox, takes it from here. She analyzes the source, then drafts the document section by section, while the stage moves from gathering to generating.

beats.caption: The agent starts building the BRD draft

steps.narration: After the BRD has been generated, you can edit content in place.

beats.caption: BRD has been generated
You can then directly edit the BRD

steps.narration: You can audit a single section to check it for gaps and internal inconsistency.

beats.caption: Or audit any section using AI

steps.narration: Or you can ask the assistant for suggestions and decide what to accept.

beats.caption: Or ask the agent for suggestions

steps.narration: Watch the AI assumption tags. Where the transcript didn't state something outright, Velox fills the gap and labels it, so you always know which lines came from the document and which came from the model.

beats.caption: The agent also flags its assumptions

steps.narration: To make changes to the BRD, you tell the assistant directly over chat.

beats.caption: You can make changes to the BRD via chat

steps.narration: Here, I'll ask it to bring automated routing and supervisor dashboards into scope.

beats.caption: You can make changes to the BRD via chat

steps.narration: Velox applies the edit, moves the session into refining, and confirms that section five was updated. You can directly open the updated section, where items have been lifted out of the out of scope list and placed into scope.

beats.caption: You can then directly head to the updated section

steps.narration: Confirm it

beats.caption: Validate and confirm the changes

steps.narration: or revert it in a single click.

beats.caption: ..or revert them, if you want

steps.narration: When the document is ready, you can download it as a Word file

beats.caption: Once done, you can download in .docx format

steps.narration: or publish it straight to your Confluence space, so the BRD lands where your delivery team already works.

beats.caption: ..or upload the BRD to your Confluence Space

steps.narration: Transcript to reviewed BRD in a single session.

timing.durationRule: Step duration is derived from its narration audio clip length, floored by minHoldSeconds when present. If narration is null, silentDurationSeconds is required and is authoritative. Beats subdivide a step: beat 0 starts at the step's first frame; each later beat starts at the frame corresponding to its atWord index in the narration's alignment data. A beat without atWord in a single-beat step starts at frame 0.
timing.referenceSecondsNote: referenceSeconds are the measured timings of the original hand-edited video. They are ignored by the timeline builder and consumed only by the validation script, which compares generated audio length against them and flags implausible authored speaking rates.
